subject: PrivNet intermittent control-plane handshake failures — investigation & customer briefing
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaclinic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@novaclinic.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane disconnects from our Private deployment (NovaClinic EU)

Evelyn —

We're seeing intermittent control-plane connection failures from our EU-private deployment since ~11:20 UTC today. Symptoms: the private agent on our side repeatedly re-establishes TLS sessions and a subset of API calls (health checks, cache prewarm) fail with handshake_error followed by a 30–90s reconnection. This spiked our job queue and caused a brief processing backlog for daytime traffic.

We've collected TCP/TLS traces and attached a pcap and conn traces (novaclinic_conn-traces-0529.zip). We rolled one node (edge-03) and saw the problem surface again on edge-07. No config changes on our side. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's control-plane side (deploys, library updates, or network rules)?

We need: an ETA for root cause and at minimum a mitigation we can apply if this recurs. Hoping to avoid a full rollback.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform, NovaClinic
Attachment: novaclinic_conn-traces-0529.zip (log bundle), handshake-pcap-0529.pcap (pcap)

Subject: PrivNet EU — initial triage notes

Evelyn / Aditya — quick notes from initial triage (INC-4923):

What we observed:
- Multiple control-plane sessions from NovaClinic agents are failing TLS handshakes before application data exchange (ClientHello -> handshake_failure).
- Failures correlate with larger initial TLS records (clients sending >10KB ClientHello extensions due to a cert/fingerprint probe we recently enabled).
- No config changes from customer side; network path shows occasional PMTU (path MTU) blackholes in AS287 (observed as fragmented IP segments dropped).

Likely hypothesis (priority):
1) New probe in agent causing larger TLS records + path MTU fragments -> some middleboxes/NACLs along the private link drop fragments, leading to handshake aborts.
2) Separate but concurrent: an infra push to a control-plane side library (BoringSSL build flags) increased sensitivity to incomplete ClientHello sequences.

Immediate mitigations to propose:
- For NovaClinic: temporarily disable the new probe (agent toggle) and roll agent with small MTU conservative setting (1420) on affected nodes.
- For Redwood infra: roll back the BoringSSL build flag change in 2 hours if customer-side mitigation does not fully resolve.

Attachments: brief pcap excerpt and a reproduction script (see INC-4923).

Ben
Ben Carter
Manager, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaclinic.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@novaclinic.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 16:18:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane disconnects from our Private deployment (NovaClinic EU)

Thanks, team. We applied the suggested mitigations on the affected nodes: disabled the new probe and set MTU to 1420 for edge-03/07/12. After the change we observed a marked reduction in handshake failures; connection stability improved within ~12 minutes. We're still monitoring for recurrences but backlog drained and processing recovered for the most part.

Two asks while you investigate root cause:
1) Please confirm whether you'll roll back the infra build flag or provide a definitive fix (we prefer not to leave our agents with probe disabled for long).
2) Draft a postmortem we can share with our execs that includes timeline, root cause hypothesis, and remediation plan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Martin Cole <mcole@edgecloud.io>
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: PrivNet EU handshake regression (INC-4923)

Alex / NovaClinic SRE / Martin —

Thanks again for working through this with us. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps — attached is a short postmortem draft (privnet-postmortem-draft-0531.pdf) with logs and a remediation timeline.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-05-29 11:18 UTC -> 2028-05-29 16:06 UTC (primary impact period).
- Impact: intermittent control-plane TLS handshake failures for a subset of NovaClinic private agents in EU; user-facing job processing backlog for ~45–90 minutes.
- Root cause (consolidated): interaction of two changes — (A) a newly enabled client-side probe that increased initial TLS ClientHello size; (B) an internal build flag change to BoringSSL that reduced acceptance of fragmented ClientHello sequences. The combination caused handshakes to abort when path MTU caused fragmentation and an intermediary dropped fragments.

Actions taken:
- Customer-side: NovaClinic disabled the probe and set conservative MTU (1420) on affected nodes — immediate improvement.
- Redwood infra: we reverted the BoringSSL build flag for EU control-plane nodes at 2028-05-29 15:45 UTC; further validation completed at 16:00 UTC.
- We created detection rules to alert on abnormal distribution of TLS ClientHello sizes and on increased handshake_failure rates (INC-4923).

Corrective and preventative items:
1) Deploy a build that tolerates fragmented ClientHello sequences and add explicit fragmentation handling tests to our CI (owner: Runtime team; ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Add a pre-deploy test that compares ClientHello size distributions in lab vs. canary and blocks large-clienthello changes (owner: Infra QA; ETA: 1 week).
3) Update customer troubleshooting docs with an MTU/fragmentation checklist and temporary mitigations (owner: Docs; ETA: 1 week).
4) Offer NovaClinic a one-time service credit for downtime and hands-on validation support during their next weekly maintenance window.

Next steps for NovaClinic: review the attached postmortem and let us know if you want a joint exec-facing summary. We'll move the items above into tracked tasks in INC-4923 and keep you updated on progress.

Apologies for the disruption. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review tomorrow to walk through traces and the remediation plan.

Best —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: privnet-postmortem-draft-0531.pdf
